# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_008_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 4

**1** When she had finished speaking she asked, "Do you want to know anything more?" I asked her, "Lady, why is the tower built upon water?" "Because," she said, "your life has been saved and will be saved through water. But the tower has been founded upon the word of the almighty and glorious Name, and it is held up by the invisible power of the Lord." **2** I said to her, "Lady, this is a great and marvelous thing. But who are the six young men who built it?" "These," she answered, "are the holy angels of God who were created first, to whom the Lord delivered all his creation to build up, increase, and rule. Through them the Lord will complete the building." **3** "And all the other people bringing stones?" "These also are holy angels of God, but the six have authority over them. The building will be completed and all will rejoice around the tower and give glory to God, because it is finished." **4** "Lady, I would like to know the fate of the stones." She replied, "The rejected stones that were not thrown far — these are those who have sinned and wish to repent. Because they have not been placed in the building, they remain nearby. If they repent, they can indeed be placed in the building. But if the tower is completed before they do repent, they will be cast out." **5** "The cracked ones — these are those who have believed hypocritically in most things; they have no genuine integrity. They blow hot and cold, and their works are wicked." **6** "Those thrown far away are the sons of lawlessness. They received the faith, but their wickedness never departed from them. Therefore they are unfit for the building and have been thrown far away because of God's wrath; their wicked deeds provoked the Lord to anger." **7** "The rest lying about in great numbers unused — the rough ones are those who knew the truth but did not remain in it and do not associate with the saints; therefore they are useless." **8** "The cracked ones are those who harbor malice against one another in their hearts and cannot be at peace with each other; but they appear peaceable on the outside, and when they separate the malice returns into their hearts. Those are the cracks in those stones." **9** "Those thrown into fire and burned — these are those who have completely departed from the living God, and repentance has not entered their hearts, because of their licentious way of life and the wickedness they have committed." **10** "Those near the water that could not roll in — these are those who heard the word and desired to be baptized in the name of the Lord; but when true holiness and the way of truth came to their minds, they changed their decision and turned back to their wicked desires." **11** She finished speaking to me about the tower. "Do not ask anymore about the tower; these words are sufficient. But take careful heed of everything I have shown you." She then spoke to the virgins: "Be diligent in building the tower, lest the master grows impatient over the delay and turns to some other means." With that she went away, and with her the young men who had been building, and the virgins who stood around the tower. I saw nothing left of the tower — only the stones lying on the ground.

---

*LOGOS note: "blow hot and cold" is the Greek idiom for instability; "sons of lawlessness" = Semitic idiom for those characterized by lawlessness.*
